summary: FidelityManager exposes live authoritative _states/_metrics on its returned facade, allowing capability holders to bypass budget/accounting and transition-fence invariants.

details.defect: The returned manager table owns writable authoritative _states and _metrics. Public methods trust those fields for capacity, level accounting, transition fencing, hold/cooldown, timestamps, and diagnostics, so any holder of the manager reference can mutate canonical manager state outside validated methods.
evidence: Manager construction stores _states and _metrics directly on the returned setmetatable facade; the Manager type definition names those backing fields as well.
register/step/unregister/getState/getMetrics read the same mutable tables; the same-entity reentrancy guard trusts state.transitioning from _states.
An applyTransition callback can close over the manager, set manager._states[entityId].transitioning = false, then call step recursively, bypassing the intended in-flight same-entity transition fence.

A capability holder can directly alter observedLevel, timestamps, registration state, or metrics, desynchronizing getState() from levelCounts/registeredEntities without passing registration or transition validation.
Current exact-head tests cover public-API reentrancy, atomicity, hostile inputs, budgets, timestamps, and frozen metric snapshots, but do not seal or adversarially probe the backing tables.
priorMiningScreen: Repository PR/issue/code searches for FidelityManager capability/private/_states/_metrics/direct mutation found no dedicated active sealing child.
PR #398 covers cross-entity public-method commit isolation, not direct mutation of the authoritative backing tables.

PR #58 is a directly analogous WorldEntity authority-boundary repair using closure-private backing state, confirming the project already treats exposed mutable authoritative tables as an architectural defect class.
HG-BACKFILL-FIDELITY PR #385 is the generation-4 integration target; capacity-mining must not mutate its production scope.

proposedChild.title: FidelityManager: seal authoritative state behind a capability-safe facade
scope: Move authoritative entity-state and mutable metric backing out of the returned manager table into closure-private or otherwise unreachable storage keyed to the manager capability.
Preserve the public FidelityManager API and exact-head observable semantics.
Add adversarial tests proving a callback/consumer cannot forge the same-entity transition fence or directly desynchronize observed state, capacity, timestamps, and metrics.
acceptance: Returned managers expose no writable authoritative state or metric control surface.
The same-entity in-flight transition fence cannot be disabled by an applyTransition callback that holds the manager reference.
Observed-level, registration-capacity, timestamp, and metric invariants change only through validated public operations.
getMetrics remains a frozen snapshot and public PR #385 behavior remains compatible.
Canonical exact-head CI and relevant Lune tests are green; no Studio/viewport evidence is claimed for this source-only child.

verification.existingEvidence: PR #385 exact-head canonical CI run 31532320675 is green for the inspected source; it predates this finding and does not validate the proposed sealing fix.
